# The centroid of the prescribed balanced moment body can miss OC

This note tests the selector: choose a weighted integer centerpoint j,
let D_j be its marginal closed-halfspace capacity, put t=D_j/2, and
take the ordinary centroid of the base-balanced moment body M_t(j).
The selector FAILS on the exact n=1,d=1 convex body below. The eligible
integer centerpoint is unique, and the prescribed mass is used exactly.

The note also determines all alternative masses t for this example.
Some work, so the example does not refute optimizing over t instead of
fixing D_j/2. It is not an OC counterexample.

## 1. The continuous half-mass screen always succeeds

For uniform volume mu on a convex body K of mass M, let M_(M/2) be
the centroids of all dominated submeasures sigma<=mu of mass M/2.
Complementation sigma -> mu-sigma preserves this mass and sends its
centroid x to 2g_K-x. Thus M_(M/2) is centrally symmetric about g_K.
It has positive interior, for example by the homothetic trimmed-body
construction in `candidate cf94bd7190201a57`.
Its ordinary centroid is exactly g_K, so ordinary Grunbaum applies.

Hence the proposed rule cannot fail in its n=0 instance. More generally,
if mu has integer first moment Mj, complementation relates the mass-t
and mass-(M-t) balanced moment bodies by reflection and homothety about
the full continuous centroid. This symmetry does not identify the
centroid of M_(D_j/2)(j) when D_j<M.

## 2. An actual rational mixed body with a unique eligible base

Put n=d=1 and prescribe three interval fibers

    K_-1=[-21/80,-13/80],
    K_0=[-1/2,1/2],
    K_1=[-59/80,5/16].                               (1)

Let C be the convex hull of these lifted intervals. The endpoint fibers
have the same continuous center s=-17/80 and lengths

    a=1/10, b=1, c=21/20,

respectively. Their Minkowski midpoint interval is [-1/2,3/40],
contained in K_0. Thus the hull has exactly the fibers (1) at its three
integer indices, and no others. It is a compact full-dimensional
polygon: a vertical segment and a point at another base already span
the plane, and its convex hull has interior. Therefore intrinsic q=1
and the actual mixed measure is the sum of these interval lengths,

    M=a+b+c=43/20.

For the one-dimensional marginal, the capacities at the three possible
bases are

    D_-1=1/10, D_0=11/10, D_1=21/20.

Every integer outside [-1,1] has capacity zero. Since M/2=43/40,
only j=0 is a weighted integer centerpoint: 44/40>M/2 but both other
capacities are smaller. The prescribed mass is consequently

    t=D_0/2=11/20.                                  (2)

There is no alternate eligible integer j that could change this
instance of the proposed rule.

## 3. Exact balanced moment-body support optimization

Let M_t(0) be the set of continuous centroids of submeasures sigma<=mu
of mass t with integer first moment zero. Base balance forces the
endpoint source masses to agree, say both are ell. The middle source
mass is t-2ell. All admissible masses therefore satisfy

    max(0,(t-1)/2)<=ell<=min(1/10,t/2),
    0<t<=T_max(0)=6/5.                               (3)

Every ell in (3) is attainable by dominated interval submeasures.
The maximum mass follows by taking the whole middle and left fibers
and a mass-1/10 submeasure of the right fiber.

For a length-w interval centered at g, a dominated submeasure of mass
m has first moment between

    mg-m(w-m)/2 and mg+m(w-m)/2.                     (4)

The upper and lower endpoints are attained by the top and bottom
subintervals of length m. The elementary threshold exchange inequality
proves optimality: moving any mass from a smaller to a larger coordinate
increases its first moment until the top interval is filled. Thus (4)
is the exact support optimization over ALL dominated submeasures,
not just uniformly thinned ones.

For fixed ell, the combined source moment has center
N(ell)=2s ell=-17ell/40 and radius Q(ell)/2, where

    Q(ell)=t(1-t)+(4t-17/20)ell-6ell^2.

Write A=t(1-t)/2 and maximize the two scalar quadratics over (3):

    F_+(t)=max_ell [(2t-17/20)ell-3ell^2],
    F_-(t)=max_ell [2t ell-3ell^2].                  (5)

Then the moment body is the compact interval

    M_t(0)=[-(A+F_-(t))/t, (A+F_+(t))/t].           (6)

Indeed (4) attains both support endpoints for each ell; maximizing over
the compact interval (3) gives attained global endpoints. The feasible
submeasure set is convex and its normalized moment map is linear at
fixed mass t, so every point between the two endpoints is attainable.
This proves the whole body (6), using the exact primal equivalent of
the base-balanced support dual, without a numerical reconstruction.

At the prescribed t=11/20, the maximizing masses in (5) are

    ell_+=1/24, ell_-=1/10,
    F_+=1/192, F_-=2/25, A=99/800.

Substitution into (6) gives

    M_(11/20)(0)=[-163/440,619/2640].                 (7)

Its ordinary centroid is the midpoint of this positive-length interval,

    y=-359/5280.                                    (8)

The selected point (0,y) belongs to the actual middle fiber, as required
by the selector definition. Its failure below is a depth failure, not
a failure of membership or of existence of the centroid.

## 4. One explicit closed ambient cap beats the OC threshold

Consider

    H={ (z,x): x<=-359/5280-(707/1056)z }.            (9)

Its boundary passes through (0,y). At z=1 its threshold is -59/80,
the lower endpoint of K_1, so it retains only that endpoint and zero
H_1 mass there. At z=-1 its threshold is 397/660, above the whole
left interval, so that fiber contributes 1/10. The middle contribution
is y+1/2. Consequently

    mu(H)=1/10+1/2-359/5280=2809/5280,
    (gamma_1/2)M=M/4=43/80=2838/5280.

The deficit is the positive rational number

    29/5280.                                       (10)

The cap is oblique and closed. Its endpoint boundary mass is zero for
the relevant H_1 measure; no open-cap substitution has been used.
This proves failure of the exact prescribed selector with its unique
weighted integer centerpoint and prescribed mass D_0/2.

## 5. All alternative masses can be checked exactly

Let y(t) be the ordinary centroid of (6), so

    y(t)=[F_+(t)-F_-(t)]/(2t).

Maximizing the quadratics in (5) by clipping their critical points
to (3) gives the complete formula

    y(t)=-t/6,                         0<t<=3/10;
    y(t)=-1/10+3/(200t),                3/10<=t<=17/40;
    y(t)=t/6-29/120+433/(9600t),         17/40<=t<=29/40;
    y(t)=-17/(400t),                    29/40<=t<=6/5.  (11)

For detail, F_- uses ell=t/3 until t=3/10, then ell=1/10. F_+ uses
ell=0 until t=17/40, then ell=(2t-17/20)/6 until t=29/40, then
ell=1/10. The lower bound (t-1)/2 in (3) never changes these maximizers:
when it is positive, both selected masses are already 1/10 and
(t-1)/2<=1/10. Thus (11) includes every feasible positive t.

There is also an exact all-halfspace depth formula for these points.
For intervals of lengths a<=c and thresholds whose sum is L above
their lower endpoints, minimizing their two retained lower lengths
over opposite threshold shifts gives

    inf_v [clamp(v,0,a)+clamp(L-v,0,c)]
       =min(a,L_+).                                (12)

If either term is saturated, their sum is at least a; if neither is
saturated, it is at least L_+. These give the lower bound, and it is
attained by assigning the whole small interval and excluding the
large one when L>=a, or by splitting L when 0<=L<=a, or by excluding
both when L<=0. The analogous upper-tail identity follows by reflection.

In (1) the sum of the endpoint lower bounds is -1, and the sum of
their upper bounds is 3/20. For every y in [-17/80,0], both relevant
quantities 2y+1 and 3/20-2y exceed a=1/10. Thus each endpoint-pair
cap infimum in (12), in either orientation, equals 1/10. The middle
fiber contributes y+1/2 or 1/2-y. Vertical ambient caps containing
base zero have mass at least D_0=11/10. Therefore the exact normalized
depth at such a point is

    depth_S((0,y))=(3/5+y)/M.                       (13)

Every y(t) lies in this interval. This follows directly from (5):
F_+<=F_-, while F_--F_+ is at most (17/20) times the largest admissible
ell, which is at most t/2. Hence -17/80<=y(t)<=0.

Equations (11)--(13) show that the selector fails OC precisely when

    2/5<t<(43+3sqrt(13))/80.                        (14)

In the second branch y<-1/16 is equivalent to t>2/5. In the third
branch the same inequality is 1600t^2-1720t+433<0, whose roots are
(43+-3sqrt(13))/80; only the upper root lies in that branch. The first
and fourth branches give no further failure. Equalities at the two
endpoints of (14) meet the OC threshold exactly.

For example, t=1/10 gives y=-1/60 and unnormalized depth 7/12, larger
than M/4 by 11/240. The original middle-fiber centroid (0,0) itself
has unnormalized depth 3/5>M/4. Thus the body obeys OC and changing
t can repair this particular instance. What is disproved is the
specified universal rule t=D_j/2 and then taking the moment body's
ordinary centroid. No assertion against every j,t selection or every
point of the common moment body is made.
